title: Credits
description: The most inspiring words of all time roll up a black screen as a film’s end credits: Roosevelt, Baldwin, Dickinson, Frost, Wilde and more, each quote a short centred block in Garamond with its author as the credit, with grain, halation and gate weave. Under it, a quiet bed of voices in the dark: a murmuring room, soft whispers drifting past on either side, and the projector you can hear speed up as you drag or scroll.
intent: One thing done like the real thing: a projected end-credits crawl of correctly attributed, much-loved lines you can grab, with capped inertia that always relaxes back to a pace slow enough to read, over a synthesised theatre ambience (formant-filtered murmur, HRTF-panned whispers, room tone, a convolution hall) that starts on the first touch and swells a little when the lights would come up.
sources: herb reference board: cfcf small white poem block, 95d9 quiet captions; herb asked for the most inspirational quotes of all time
